extracted.intended_audience: Investigators applying for AHRQ research grants and peer reviewers / review officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on how AHRQ grant applications are evaluated by peer review panels, including reviewer selection, SRO responsibilities, scoring rules, core and additional review criteria, and summary/streamlining procedures. Intended to inform both applicants and reviewers about expectations and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are selected to participate in the peer review groups based on a number of considerations, including: Authorities in their scientific fields; Dedication to high quality, fair, and even-handed reviews; Demonstration of their abilities to work collegially in a group setting; Experience in grant/contract review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRO nominates reviewers based on broad input from the scientific community, AHRQ program staff, and experts who have served as peer reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: A Scientific Review Officer (SRO) is the Designated Federal Official of the peer review group meeting. Her/his role is to make sure that each application receives a review that is thorough, competent and fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRO oversees, coordinates and administers the peer review process; enforces AHRQ principles/rules for review; performs initial administrative and technical review of applications for completeness and accuracy; nominates reviewers; works with the peer review group chairperson; prepares summary statements after meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review meeting conduct requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure the peer review meeting is fair and yields high quality reviews, the peer review meeting should include: Balanced and adequate scientific discussion that supports the review group's recommendations; Consistent, criteria-based scoring; Adequate attention to protection of human subjects and inclusion of priority populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRO and chairperson are responsible for ensuring these elements are observed during the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statement contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the peer review meeting, the SRO prepares summary statements for all applications. The summary statement contains: Resume and summary of discussion; Minimally-edited reviewers' critiques; Final overall Impact score and percentile ranking; Budget recommendations; Administrative notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement is official feedback to the applicant conveying the issues, critiques, and/or comments raised during the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining / Triaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Streamlining is a practice through which less competitive grant applications, as judged by the study section members, are not discussed at the review meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order for an application to be streamlined, there must be unanimous agreement amongst study section members. These applications do not receive an overall impact score. For 'NOT DISCUSSED' applications, the summary statement integrates all of the written reviews from the assigned reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring system: 9-point scale and non-numeric options
rubrics_metrics.description: The AHRQ grant application scoring system uses a 9-point scale for the overall impact score and individual scores for five core criteria. Ratings are in whole numbers only (no decimal ratings). Non-numeric score options: DF = Deferred, AB = Abstention, CF = Conflict, NP = Not Present, ND = Not Discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A score of 1 indicates an exceptionally strong application with essentially no weaknesses; a score of 9 indicates an application with serious and substantive weaknesses with very few strengths; a score of 5 is considered average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score descriptors and additional guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mapping of numeric scores to qualitative descriptors and additional guidance on strengths/weaknesses: 1 Exceptional (Exceptionally strong with no weaknesses); 2 Outstanding (Outstanding); 3 Excellent (Very strong with only some minor weaknesses); 4 Very Good (Strong but with numerous minor weaknesses); 5 Good (Strong but with at least one moderate weakness); 6 Satisfactory (Some strengths but also some moderate weaknesses); 7 Fair (Some strengths but with at least one major weakness); 8 Marginal (A few strengths and a few major weaknesses); 9 Poor (Very few strengths and numerous major weaknesses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these descriptors to communicate the nature and severity of strengths/weaknesses in the critique and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weakness severity definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor Weakness: An easily addressable weakness that does not substantially lessen impact. Moderate Weakness: A weakness that lessens impact. Major Weakness: A weakness that severely limits impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should apply these definitions when characterizing critique points and determining scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall impact (definition and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score and critique to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assessment should consider the five core review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable). Note that an application does not need to be strong in all categories to be judged likely to have major scientific impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core review criterion: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this study address an important problem? If the aims of the application are achieved, how will scientific knowledge or clinical practice be advanced? What will be the effect of these studies on the concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess potential to advance the field and address an important problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core review criterion: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the PD/PI and other key personnel appropriately trained and well suited to carry out this work? Is the work proposed appropriate to the experience level(s) of the principal investigator(s) and other researchers? Does the PD/PI and investigative team bring complementary and integrated expertise to the project (if applicable)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider qualifications, appropriateness of team composition, and whether experience matches project needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core review criterion: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the project original and innovative? For example, does the project challenge existing paradigms or clinical practice; address an innovative hypothesis or critical barrier to progress in the field? Does the project develop or employ novel concepts, approaches or methodologies, tools, or technologies for this area?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovation can include challenging paradigms, addressing critical barriers, or using novel methods/tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core review criterion: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the conceptual or clinical framework, design, methods, and analyses adequately developed, well-integrated, well-reasoned, and appropriate to the aims of the project? Does the applicant acknowledge potential problem areas and consider alternative tactics?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate rigor, feasibility, integration of methods, consideration of pitfalls and alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core review criterion: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do(es) the scientific environment(s) in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success? Do the proposed studies benefit from unique features of the scientific environment(s), or subject populations, or employ useful collaborative arrangements? Is there evidence of institutional support?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional resources, collaborations, unique populations/sites, and evidence of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Protection of Human Subjects from Research Risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The involvement of human subjects and protections from research risk relating to their participation in the proposed research will be assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the 'Human Subjects Sections' of the PHS398 Research Plan component of the SF424 (R&R) for details on how human subjects protections are evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Adequacy of plans to address the needs of both genders, racial and ethnic minorities (and subgroups). Adequacy of attention to AHRQ priority populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether inclusion plans appropriately address gender, racial/ethnic diversity, and AHRQ priority populations, per NOFO and required federal citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposed budget reasonable and is the requested period of support appropriate in relation to the proposed research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget reasonableness is considered in determining scientific and technical merit, though not given a separate numeric score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Privacy and Security Protections for Patients
rubrics_metrics.description: The resources and processes to be used to address privacy and security issues in the development and implementation of the intervention will be assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should evaluate proposed plans for protecting patient privacy and data security as applicable to the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Degree of Responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: How well does the application address the purpose and objectives of the NOFO? Does the proposed project fit within an AHRQ Research Portfolio area? How responsive is the application to the special eligibility criteria, including the project requirements, noted in the NOFO?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess alignment with NOFO goals and specific program priorities; responsiveness affects overall merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criterion: Resubmission Applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group adequate? Are the improvements in the resubmission application appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For resubmissions, reviewers should evaluate whether prior concerns were addressed and whether revisions are substantive and adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration: Importance and Impact (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the importance of the problem addressed and the potential impact of the solution of this problem on health or on health care delivery?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider public health or health care delivery implications when applicable to the NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review consideration: Data Sharing Plan (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the proposed data sharing plan or the rationale for not sharing research data reasonable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, evaluate the adequacy of data sharing plans or the justification for withholding data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final overall impact score calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The final overall impact score reflects the average impact scores provided by each individual members and multiplying the average by 10; the final overall impact/priority score is reported on the summary statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, final overall impact/priority scores range from 10 (high impact) through 90 (low impact). Abstaining reviewers and those in conflict with the application and/or not present during the discussion do not provide a score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile calculation and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile, based on the final overall impact score, is an application's rank relative to other applications that are reviewed by the same scientific review group at 3 consecutive meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AHRQ calculates percentiles based on combined overall impact scores from the study section at the review meeting and the same study section at the previous two meetings (the 'base'). Percentile ratings are calculated only for discussed applications. Percentiles range from 0.1 to 100.0; lower numbers represent better scores and are used to normalize scores across peer review groups.
